title: Polynomial-time additive-error estimation of output probabilities for shallow quantum circuits
abstract: We give a deterministic classical algorithm that estimates $|\langle x|U|0^n\rangle|^2$ to additive error $\varepsilon$ in $\mathrm{poly}(n, 1/\varepsilon)$ time, where $U$ is a constant-depth quantum circuit comprised of gates with bounded fan-in and arbitrary connectivity, and $x$ is an arbitrary $n$-bit output string. This improves over prior state-of-the-art algorithms that takes $n^{O(log(n))}$ time for the same task, $n^{O(log(log(n))}$ when $U$ is geometrically local, and $n^{O(1)}$ for 2D geometrically-local circuits.

bite.hook: A new deterministic classical algorithm estimates output probabilities of shallow quantum circuits in poly time.
tldr: Researchers developed a deterministic classical algorithm to estimate quantum circuit output probabilities to an additive error.
They focused on constant-depth quantum circuits with bounded fan-in and arbitrary connectivity.
The new approach improves significantly over prior state-of-the-art super-polynomial time algorithms.
bite.whyItMatters: Showing that classical computers can efficiently simulate certain shallow quantum circuits helps define the true boundary where quantum computers gain a definitive advantage.
bite.eli5: Even though quantum computers are powerful, scientists found a regular computer shortcut that can quickly guess the outcome of certain shallow quantum setups, beating previous slow methods.
